# StarRupture game-update pipeline

Workflows that watch Steam for a new StarRupture build, check that the loader and plugins still compile (one result per component), and check the new client build offline. They run on GitHub-hosted runners with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`. No self-hosted runner. Issues are used only as alerts: `vmap-watchdog.yml`, the `alert` jobs of `sr-client-check.yml` and `sr-watch.yml` (the latter for a failed poll or compile check, posted to the same per-branch issue) and the stale-PR step of `sr-watch.yml`. The issue "SR map mode: <branch> needs attention" is opened on the first problem and commented on for every later one; it carries the label `pipeline-alert`, is assigned to the owner and mentions him, so GitHub notifies him, and each alert line says its cause (the failing job or gate and its first error line, or the verdict reason). Alert lines: a failed job; a client check that did not run (status `skipped` or `no-login`); a map-mode HOLD for any reason but "nothing new" or the autopilot switch alone; map rows that were not pushed to the loader fork; a candidate loader that failed to build or pass its tests; a client rig that did not end with success and PASS; a newer release of a pinned third-party plugin waiting for review (loud, but it blocks nothing). A HOLD whose only reason is "autopilot is disabled", with every gate and job passing, is not an alert: the alert job writes one "Ready, publish held (autopilot off)" comment on the update PR (edited in place) and no issue. A run with no alert line labels the PR `chain-passed-<branch>`; when `sr-watch.yml` skips a build because its game-update PR is open and that PR has been open over 6 hours without the label for every changed client branch, it comments on (or opens) the branch's alert issue, at most once per 6 hours. The one secret is the Steam login of a separate CI account, used only by the client check (see "Steam login for the client check").

They live in `msantoro12/starrupture-ci`. The mod repos are checked out from `vars.MOD_OWNER` (default `AlienXAXS`); nothing here writes to them.

```
.github/workflows/sr-watch.yml        Steam watcher
.github/workflows/sr-build-all.yml    compile check
.github/workflows/sr-client-check.yml offline check of a new client build
.github/sr-pipeline/poll-steam.mjs    the polling script sr-watch runs
.github/sr-pipeline/README.md         this file
state/steam.json                      recorded build ids (baseline, on main)
```

## What runs when

| Workflow | Trigger | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `sr-watch.yml` | cron at :07 and :37 every hour; manual (`force` input) | Polls api.steamcmd.net for app 1631270 and app 3809400 (every branch without a password, for both), plus the newest Steam news title. Retries 3 times per app, then skips that app for the run (warning annotation, no PR). First sight of an app: commits the baseline to `main`, no alert. On a real change against `state/steam.json` on main: pushes a `game-update/<app>-<branch>-<buildid>` branch holding the new ids, opens a PR titled `Game build <id> on <branch>` (label `game-update`) whose body has the changed-build table, the newest news title and the per-component checklist, then runs `sr-build-all.yml` with the PR number and, for each changed client branch, `sr-client-check.yml`. If a `game-update/*` PR is already open, it is updated instead of duplicated; an unchanged build is not re-announced. |
| `sr-build-all.yml` | nightly 03:23 UTC; manual (branch per repo, default `main`; optional `pr`); called by `sr-watch.yml` | `interface-check` (Plugin SDK `PLUGIN_INTERFACE_VERSION` against the loader's `[MIN, MAX]`), `loader` (Client Release and Server Release), `plugin` (BetterDrone, BetterCheats, WAILA, Codex), `report`. Fail-fast is off. Optional `loader_repo` (blank: the default owner's `StarRupture-ModLoader`) builds the loader from `msantoro12/StarRupture-ModLoader` or `AlienXAXS/StarRupture-ModLoader` only, and `loader_branch` also takes a full commit sha; this is how the rig's `loader-client` candidate is built from a fork branch. `report` writes the job summary and, when a PR number was given, posts the same table as a PR comment: one row per component with status, job link and artifact link, and a static "Game SDK: manual" row. Artifacts hold build outputs only, 3 days retention. |
| `sr-client-check.yml` | called by `sr-watch.yml` per changed client branch (a forced run checks both); manual (`branch`, optional `pr`); weekly Monday 06:17 UTC (login age only) | `build-scanner` builds `sr-aobscan-client.exe` from `loader_repo`@`loader_ref` (default AlienXAXS `main`: the released line is what players run and what reads the feed, so the patterns are the live ones, and the same commit is what the map rows are cut from) with `tools/AobScan` from `scanner_repo`@`scanner_ref` (default the fork's `ci/aobscan`, which holds only that tool), and reads the loader's required CL (a loader with a version map has none) and the pinned Game SDK's `Offsets::`. `check` (environment `steam-client`) restores the saved steamcmd login, downloads the client build with Valve's steamcmd (`app_update 1631270`, `-beta <branch>` for a branch other than public; steamcmd cannot fetch single files, so it is the full build, about 16-17 GB down and 50 GB on disk), deletes steamcmd and the login cache, then checks the exe: the loader's version gate passes (ProductVersion ends with the required CL; for a loader with a version map, the running CL has a row in its `kBuilds`, as `sr-aobscan` reports from the loader's own gate code in `exe.supported`; a loader with neither fails; with `map_mode` on, a build whose gate says no is a new build, recorded as status `new-build` and measured by map mode instead of failing the check, and with `map_mode` off it still fails), every PreflightRegistry pattern resolves (sr-aobscan; the required ones decide pass or fail), and the four Game-SDK globals (GObjects, FName::AppendString, GNames, GWorld) are compared with the SDK's `Offsets::`. `plugin-plan` lists the plugins: each `plugins` entry is `owner/repo@ref` (built from source) or `owner/repo@latest-release` (the repository's latest GitHub release, resolved through the API to its tag, which the report shows; default: MiniMap, from its author LetMeInside). A plugin owned by msantoro12 is built in the `plugins` job; another author's, and the default nine at AlienXAXS `main`, are fetched or built by the `check` job itself, never stored as an artifact, and validated only (see "Adding your plugin to CI"). Owners are msantoro12 and AlienXAXS, plus LetMeInside for `@latest-release`, which for another author's plugin means its reviewed release (the Pin in `ci/plugin-names.json`, see "Policy for the unattended path"), never its newest; that code runs on the runner with the same trust as `scanner_ref`. After the login cache is deleted, `sr-aobscan --plugin` runs each plugin's `OnPluginLoadHooks` against the downloaded exe through the loader's own hook scanner. Verdicts: PASS; GAME-CALL (partial coverage, never a full pass: every pattern registered before the first game call resolved, and the calls into game code, which cannot run offline, were stopped and the hook resumed; reads "N/N resolved before first game call; later scans not exercised"); FAIL (any recorded pattern MISSING or AMBIGUOUS: the loader refuses the plugin; a row the second run, with the scan cache warm, answered differently; or a request that resolved whose own pattern does not match the exe exactly once, labelled OWN-MISSING or OWN-AMBIGUOUS, which a map row would otherwise hide); CRASH (a fault in the plugin's own code, or a game call before any pattern resolved); REFUSED (interface version outside the loader's range); NONE (no `OnPluginLoadHooks`); BUILD-FAILED, FETCH-FAILED, ERROR. PASS, GAME-CALL and NONE count as pass. Limit: when a stopped game call returns null and the plugin bails out, every later scan and failure report is skipped, so GAME-CALL can hide a pattern the hook registers only after a successful call (in game the loader would refuse the plugin); it can also read GAME-CALL for a call that would fail in game. Beside the patterns, `Check the fixed offsets` reads each built plugin's source against the PDB layout of the checked build and of the public one: every offset a plugin reads at a raw number and lists in `ci/native-keys.txt` with an anchor must equal the PDB's, or the plugin fails as `OFFSETS` (`OFFSETS-UNCHECKED` when the layout report is missing). The fix step rewrites an offset when one constant is right for every build that matters, and leaves the rest failing. A failing plugin shows in `result.json` under `plugins.status`; the top-level `status` covers the loader only. Artifact `client-check-<branch>` (result.json and the scanner output, 14 days). `report` comments the result on the PR, with the age of the saved login. `sr-watch.yml` passes `STEAM_CI_USERNAME` and `STEAM_CI_LOGIN_CACHE` by name: a called job sees an environment secret only when its caller passes it, and both are `required` in `workflow_call`. Without the login the `check` job fails with the cause, in the job log, the PR comment and the alert issue; it never skips green, and map mode does not run. The watcher does not check a build again while its update PR is open. To run the compile and client checks of an open update PR again, dispatch `gh workflow run sr-watch.yml --ref main -f force=true` (with no new build id it checks every recorded client branch). `login-expiry` (weekly) goes red when the saved login is within 30 days of its assumed 200-day lifetime. Map mode (`map_mode`, which `sr-watch.yml` always passes) produces the candidate with nobody's help: `map-mode` writes the new build's rows into the loader's `version_map.generated.h`, runs decide, and on a clean update exports and TEST-signs the feed and stages the build. `state/autopilot.json` gates publishing only: with `enabled: false` decide still says HOLD ("autopilot is disabled"), but the chain runs on to the export, the TEST signature and the staging (`decide.mjs --candidate`; any other HOLD reason still stops it before the export), and the `publish` job is skipped. For a build the chain carried through to staging the `push-loader` job (environment `fork-push`, secret `SR_DEPLOYKEY_MODLOADER`, passed by name from `sr-watch.yml`) pushes `auto/update-<CL>` to msantoro12/StarRupture-ModLoader: one commit on the AlienX commit the run scanned (checked out from `loader_repo`, never from the fork's own branches), changing only that header; it never pushes a tag or another branch, leaves a branch that already holds the same tree alone, and fails with the secret's name when the key is not set (owner setup: `ci/MAP-MODE.md`, step 26). Its outputs `branch` and `sha` are for the next steps; a build first seen on `public` is pushed too. The `candidate-loader` job then builds that exact loader commit (Client Release, tag `cand-<run id>-<sha7>`, through the shared action `.github/actions/build-loader`, which `sr-build-all.yml` also uses), runs the loader's `VersionMapTests` and `LayoutCheckTests`, and uploads `loader-candidate-<branch>` in the rig's candidate layout; outputs `artifact`, `version`, `expect` and `sha`. `build-scanner` also builds and runs the scanner's `ObservedTests`. The `map-mode` job outputs `expect_refused`: the plugins the loader refuses on that branch's build (the loader's own off-build rule, e.g. MiniMap, built for interface v70, on CL-129402), as the rig's `expect_refused` input; see `ci/MAP-MODE.md`. The client rig is then a required gate on that candidate: `rig-branch` and `rig-other` call `sr-client-rig.yml` one after the other (see "Client test rig"), `rig-gate` writes both verdicts into the run summary and fails the run unless both passed, and `publish` needs both rigs at verdict `PASS`. |
| `sr-client-rig.yml` | manual; called by another workflow in this repository | Launches the real game client on a hosted Windows runner under the real Steam client and judges the loader's log with `ci/verdict.ps1 -Client`: do the mods load. No schedule, no pull request trigger. See "Client test rig". |

Merging the update PR into main means the update is handled: it advances `state/steam.json`, so the watcher stops reporting that build.

### Update path per component

Release lines are always manual, need the owner's OK, and are versioned independently from each repo's own `version` file.

| Component | Today | Later phase hooks in at |
|---|---|---|
| Loader (Client) | compile check; offline client check (`sr-client-check.yml`): CL, pattern scan, SDK globals | n/a |
| Loader (Server) | compile check; placeholder step "Pattern scan" in the `loader` job | that step (the AOB scan tool) |
| BetterDrone, BetterCheats, WAILA, Codex | rebuild against the current SDK (the `plugin` job); offline pattern check of the built DLL (`sr-client-check.yml`) | a sibling job that `needs: plugin` |
| MiniMap (its author's latest release) | offline pattern check of its reviewed release's DLL (`sr-client-check.yml`, `plugins` as `@latest-release`, resolved to the Pin); also one of the rig's ten plugins (its reviewed release, pinned in `ci/plugin-names.json`, from LetMeInside/StarRupture-Plugin-MiniMap) | n/a |
| Game SDK | manual dump from a running game | n/a |

## Adding your plugin to CI

CI checks a plugin's patterns against every new StarRupture client build, offline, before any player has the build. Opting in takes one entry in `sr-client-check.yml`; this section says which entry, what is then checked, and how to read a failure.

### Opt in

A plugin is one entry in the `plugins` input of `sr-client-check.yml` (the `workflow_call` default, which `sr-watch.yml` uses, and the `workflow_dispatch` default). Change both defaults in a pull request to this repository. The plugin's `name` in the report is the repository name without `StarRupture-Plugin-`, and a name may be listed only once.

| Source | Checks | Entry | Allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@ref` | the plugin built from source at a ref | `owner/StarRupture-Plugin-Name@ref`, space-separated | owner `msantoro12` or `AlienXAXS`; `ref` is a branch, a tag or a full 40-character commit (resolved to its commit before any plugin code runs) |
| `@latest-release` | the repository's latest GitHub release, as players get it | `owner/StarRupture-Plugin-Name@latest-release` | owner `msantoro12`, `AlienXAXS` or `LetMeInside` |

A plugin in `plugins` is built on a Windows runner: the repository root has exactly one `.sln`, `Client Release|x64` builds, and exactly one DLL lands in `build\Client Release\Plugins`. The build gets `GameSDKRoot` and `PluginSDKInclude` (the Game SDK at `game_sdk_repo` / `game_sdk_ref`, default AlienXAXS `main`; the Plugin SDK at `plugin_sdk_repo` / `plugin_sdk_ref`, default AlienXAXS `main`, the released line), the loader's own `plugin_interface.h`, and `ModLoaderBuildTag` from a `version` file at the repository root (`dev` without one). A plugin that does not build fails only itself (`BUILD-FAILED`).

`@latest-release` is resolved when the run starts, through GitHub's `releases/latest` API for the repository, which skips drafts and pre-releases (a repository with no published release, or a lookup that fails, fails only that plugin as `FETCH-FAILED`; the other plugins are still checked). The word `latest-release` is reserved, so a branch or tag of that name cannot be used as an `@ref`. The report and `result.json` show the resolved tag (and its commit for a build), so a run says which release it checked. If the release has exactly one `.dll` asset, that asset is what is checked: it is downloaded on the runner and compared with the SHA-256 GitHub recorded for it (a mismatch is `FETCH-FAILED`), so the plugin is checked as players run it, not as CI would build it. If there is no `.dll` asset or more than one, the tag's source is built instead, exactly as a plugin in `@ref` is (`BUILD-FAILED` if it does not build, for instance when the source needs a header the SDK refs do not have; MiniMap's v1.2.0 source did not build in a trial run (a missing include), so for MiniMap the release DLL is what can be checked), and the report says "built from source".

**CI is validation only for another author's plugin.** Anything not owned by msantoro12 (MiniMap, or an `AlienXAXS` plugin) is only read and scanned. It is never published, uploaded, tagged or released: the `plugins` job (which makes the artifact that carries a plugin DLL between jobs) does not handle it (nor any release DLL), the `check` job fetches or builds it on its own runner after the Steam login is deleted, and the files go away with the runner. No workflow here creates a release, tag or Nexus upload for a plugin or writes to a plugin's repository except the auto-apply job's pushes of verified fixes to the owner's nine forks (`sr-build-all.yml` and `engine-test.yml` keep their builds only as workflow artifacts of this repository); the auto-apply job's deploy keys exist only for the nine plugin forks it names and it checks the plugin name and repository before pushing; and the result artifact holds reports (verdicts, scans, and for a failing plugin a proposed patch of its source), never a plugin binary. A fix for another author's plugin is only a patch in the report, for its author to take or leave.

Both sources run on the runner that held the Steam login, so the same trust applies as to the scanner (`scanner_ref`): only the owners above.

An optional second list, `ci/native-keys.txt`, names game members a plugin reads at a fixed offset (`<plugin name> Class::Member [file-suffix:regex]`; `<plugin name> ClassName [size] [optional]` names an unreflected struct whose size is written as a class-key row). They are compared with the PDB layout of the checked build and the public one (see "Check the fixed offsets" in the table above); a mismatch fails the plugin as `OFFSETS`.

### What CI checks on each game build

For each client branch that changed (`public`, `public_test_branch`), `sr-client-check.yml` downloads the build, deletes the Steam login, and runs the plugin's own `OnPluginLoadHooks` against the exe with `sr-aobscan --plugin`. The plugin's real code runs and calls the loader's own scan code, so every pattern it registers is judged the way the loader judges it in game. Game code is never started: a call into the game is stopped and the hook carries on.

1. **A cold scan.** The scan cache is empty, as on a first launch. Every recorded pattern must resolve to exactly one address of the right kind (`MISSING`: none; `AMBIGUOUS`: several; `WRONGKIND`; `BADREQUEST`). Any failure, required or declared optional, refuses the plugin, as the loader would. A miss on a key a declared feature lists turns that feature off instead and is shown as `FEATURES OFF`.
2. **The warm/cold comparison.** The hook runs again with the scan cache the first run filled, as on the next launch. Every row must come out the same (same result, same address). A difference fails the plugin.
3. **Own-pattern uniqueness.** For every request that resolved, the plugin's own pattern is counted on this exe. It must match exactly once, whatever resolved the request, including a map row. Otherwise the row is labelled `OWN-MISSING` (no match) or `OWN-AMBIGUOUS` (two or more) and the plugin fails. The row's `result` stays `OK`; the label is in the table, in the JSON row's `ownPattern` and in the note. A call that lists alternatives (`ResolveRequiredUnique`, `ResolveOptionalUnique`) is not graded on one of them, since only one has to match.
4. **The map rows.** A request carrying a map key is answered by the loader's version map before its own pattern is tried: with a row for the running build, the row's pattern decides and the plugin's own pattern is not scanned; for a build with no row, the latest row's pattern is rescanned together with the plugin's own. The report prints the `[Map]` line saying which locator took the address. On a build other than the one the plugin was built for, the note also says whether the loader would admit the plugin there (it must be built for interface 72 or later and declare `PLUGIN_MAP_MIGRATED`, and a plugin that declares it must take the Game-SDK globals in `PluginInit`).

The second run, the map resolve, the feature handling and the own-pattern grading are in the loader fork's scanner branch `ci/aobscan`, the default `scanner_repo` and `scanner_ref`, so a default run does all of the steps. It holds only `tools/AobScan`, laid over the loader named by `loader_repo` and `loader_ref` (AlienXAXS `main`), and does not build on its own.

Each plugin's verdict goes to the PR comment (one row, then a collapsible table of its patterns) and to `result.json` under `plugins`. A failing plugin fails only itself: the loader's verdict is unchanged. PASS, GAME-CALL and NONE count as pass.

### When a plugin fails

| Verdict or label | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `FAIL`, row `MISSING` | the pattern matches nowhere in this build: the game code it describes changed | write a new pattern from the new build. CI proposes replacements in the PR comment. For the owner's own plugin forks it also applies a high-confidence proposal, rebuilds, rescans on this build and the public one, and pushes a verified fix to the fork as `auto/update-<CL>` |
| `FAIL`, row `AMBIGUOUS` | the pattern matches two or more places | lengthen it with bytes unique to the function, fewer wildcards, until it matches once |
| `FAIL`, label `OWN-MISSING` | the request resolved (a map row carried it) but the plugin's own pattern matches nothing on this build | the loader has a row you do not control; a loader without that row refuses the plugin. Replace the pattern in the source |
| `FAIL`, label `OWN-AMBIGUOUS` | the same, but the pattern matches several places: it passes only because the map is carrying it | lengthen the pattern until it matches exactly once on every build CI checks (the checked build and the public one) |
| `FAIL`, "second run ... then ..." in the note | the result depended on the scan cache | the pattern's result changed once the cache was warm: make the scan deterministic (one pattern or one candidate list that always agrees) |
| `CRASH` | a fault in the plugin's own code in `OnPluginLoadHooks`, or a call into the game before any pattern resolved | keep `OnPluginLoadHooks` to resolving patterns; touch game state in `PluginInit` or later |
| `REFUSED` | `interface_version` is outside the loader's `[MIN, MAX]` | rebuild against the loader's current `plugin_interface.h` |
| `GAME-CALL` | partial coverage, counted as pass: the patterns before the first game call resolved, later scans were not exercised | none needed; to cover the rest, register the patterns before the first call into game code |
| `NONE` | no `OnPluginLoadHooks` export, nothing to check | none |
| `OFFSETS`, `OFFSETS-UNCHECKED` | a fixed offset does not match this build's PDB, or could not be checked | change the constant, or add the member to `ci/native-keys.txt` |
| `BUILD-FAILED`, `FETCH-FAILED`, `ERROR` | the plugin did not build, its release DLL could not be fetched or did not match GitHub's recorded SHA-256, or the scan could not run | see the job log |

To reproduce a result, run the scanner the workflow builds (the artifact `sr-aobscan-client-<branch>`) on an exe and your DLL: `sr-aobscan-client.exe <exe> --plugin <dll>`; add `--json` for the rows with their match counts.

## Build arguments

Copied from the loader's `release.yml` and the plugins' `release.yml` build steps (the same arguments `tools/sr-update.ps1` uses), minus everything that tags, releases or uploads. The loader builds against the Game SDK commit its submodule pins, so `game_sdk_branch` only affects plugins.

## Permissions

`permissions: {}` at the top of each workflow; each job asks for what it needs.

| Job | Permissions | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `sr-watch` / `poll` | `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, `issues: write` | baseline commit to main, `game-update/*` branches, label, PR, the stale-PR alert issue |
| `sr-watch` / `build-all` (caller) | `contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`, `actions: read` | covers the called workflow |
| `sr-build-all` / `interface`, `loader`, `plugin` | `contents: read` | check out and build |
| `sr-build-all` / `report` | `contents: read`, `actions: read`, `pull-requests: write` | list jobs and artifacts, comment on the PR |
| `sr-watch` / `alert` | `contents: read`, `issues: write`, `actions: read`, `checks: read` | a failed poll or compile check: the failed steps, their annotations and logs, the alert issue |
| `sr-watch` / `client-check` (caller) | `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, `issues: write`, `actions: write`, `checks: read` (a ceiling) | covers the called workflow (`actions: write` is the feed-loader-cleanup job's); passes `STEAM_CI_USERNAME`, `STEAM_CI_LOGIN_CACHE` (by name), `VMAP_SIGN_KEY_TEST`, `VMAP_SIGN_KEY` (the release key, read only by the publish job) and the deploy keys of the loader fork and the nine plugin forks, and `publish: true` |
| `sr-client-check` / `build-scanner` | `contents: read` | check out the loader, build the scanner |
| `sr-client-check` / `check` | `contents: read`, environment `steam-client` | the only job that can read the Steam login; checks out no repository |
| `sr-client-check` / `report` | `contents: read`, `pull-requests: write` | comment on the PR; no environment, no secrets |
| `sr-client-check` / `alert` | `contents: read`, `issues: write`, `pull-requests: write`, `actions: read`, `checks: read` | the alert issue, the `chain-passed-<branch>` label and ready note on the PR, the failed steps, annotations and logs of the run |
| `sr-client-check` / `login-expiry` | none | reads the repo variable `STEAM_CI_LOGIN_AT` |
| `sr-client-rig` / `rig` | `contents: read`, `actions: read`, environment `steam-client` | the one job; reads the Steam login in the install, launch and leak-gate steps only; `actions: read` is for fetching a candidate run's artifact |

The repo setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" must be on (Settings, Actions, General, or `gh api -X PUT repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/permissions/workflow -f default_workflow_permissions=read -F can_approve_pull_request_reviews=true`).

## Steam login for the client check

The client check logs in with a separate Steam account that owns StarRupture, never the owner's main account. Its password never reaches CI: `steam-ci-login.ps1` (on the owner's PC) runs Valve's steamcmd from a private folder, the owner types the password and the Steam Guard code into steamcmd's own prompt, and the script saves steamcmd's login cache (`config/config.vdf`, whose `ConnectCache` entry holds the refresh token), base64-encoded, to:

- Bitwarden Secrets Manager, project `dev`: `STEAM_CI_USERNAME`, `STEAM_CI_LOGIN_CACHE`
- this repo's environment `steam-client` (deployment branch: `main` only): the same two secrets
- repo variable `STEAM_CI_LOGIN_AT`: the date of the login, for the expiry warning

`-Renew` does the same fresh login (password and Steam Guard code again) for the account name saved in Bitwarden. When a run fails with "login expired, run steam-ci-login.ps1 -Renew", do that. The workflow has no `pull_request` trigger and the environment only serves `main`, so the login is never reachable from a pull request or another branch. In the `check` job the decoded token values and the account name are masked, account ids are cut from the steamcmd output, and steamcmd with its cache is deleted before the scanner runs. That does not isolate the scanner: it runs in the same job, whose process holds the secret in memory. So whoever can push to the loader branches it is built from (`loader_ref`, `scanner_ref`; `loader_repo` is limited to `msantoro12` or `AlienXAXS`) can reach the Steam login, as can whoever can push to `main` here. The `check` job runs only the scanner `build-scanner` made in the same run (SHA-256 checked).

To revoke: delete the environment `steam-client` (and the Bitwarden secrets) and deauthorize the account's devices at store.steampowered.com/twofactor/manage.

## Client test rig

`sr-client-rig.yml` answers one question: do the mods load. Given a loader and plugin set and a Steam branch, it installs the game client with steamcmd, signs the real Steam client in with the saved login (the one `sr-client-check.yml` uses; no password), launches the game with `-nullrhi -unattended -nosound -log` and the loader's `modloader.ini` set to `[AutoUpdate] Enabled=0`, `[Logging] Level=INFO`, `[UI] Enabled=0`, stops it a minute after `Boot sequence finished` and judges the result with `ci/verdict.ps1 -Client`: every DLL still the file that went in, the loader and each plugin at the expected version and loaded, no plugin loaded that is not in the set, no crash dialog or crash file, the game alive at the end (a `boot.json` that lacks those fields fails). A compatibility report is judged by what it says, not by existing: it fails on outcome `safe-off`, a required pattern miss, an unresolved or rejected global, a changed member that is `missing` or a `vtableSlot`, a feature switched off or a report that is listed but cannot be read; a `partial` report, or an `unchanged` one (format 4: the layout did not move and a plugin's size request wrote the report), with only moved members passes and shows them as a note (for example `layout moved: UCrEnviroWaveTimerSubsystem::TimerActor 0x90->0x98`). The report's optional `sizes` array has one entry per struct-size request (`plugin`, `key`, `rowCL`, `rowSize`, `reflectedSize`, `result`), which is the version map's class-key row against the size the running game reflects. Each entry becomes a note line (`size row <plugin>: <key> row 0x2C (CL-129402), reflected 0x2C: match`); `mismatch` and `no-row` (an unreflected struct with no row) fail, `row-only` (unreflected, row present) and `reflected-only` (no row for this build) pass as notes, and a result that contradicts its own sizes, an unknown result or a malformed entry fails. A report with no `sizes`, or an empty one, is judged as before. A plugin whose init needs the UI layer the rig turns off (`UiOffInitFailure` in `ci/plugin-names.json`, today MiniMap's atlas error) passes as loaded when its log holds that one ERROR line and `Plugin initialization failed` for it and nothing else, and one fewer plugin is expected to initialise; any other ERROR, init failure, crash or refusal still fails. A plugin may be declared refused only for its own refusal lines; a fault or crash line fails it regardless. A Steam `Application load error` on the first launch is retried (at most twice, recorded in `boot.json`); nothing else is.

The set is the loader's client zip and each of ten plugins' `<Name>-Client.dll` from the Latest GitHub release of each repo (or the tag given in `tags`), kept in the Actions cache; the one exception is a plugin of another author, which runs only at a reviewed release (see "Policy for the unattended path"). The ten are BetterCheats, BetterDrone, CameraControls, Codex, Compass, ProductionViewer, RuptureTimer, WAILA and WaveOptimiser (AlienXAXS, or `MOD_OWNER`) and MiniMap, whose source repo is LetMeInside/StarRupture-Plugin-MiniMap (its author's, not ours): its release carries `MiniMap-Client.dll` beside a zip and a manifest, only the DLL is picked, and it is cached like the others (asset id and digest in the key), but fetched by its pinned tag, not at Latest. MiniMap reports `Plugin info - Name: MiniMap` with its version without the tag's leading `v` (release `v1.2.0`, log `1.2.0`), so the rig expects that form (`StripV` in `ci/plugin-names.json`, with `Owner`). It is built for plugin interface v70, so the loader loads it on CL-127004 and refuses it on CL-129402: a refusal on a build the loader runs is a fail, and on CL-129402 it passes only when `expect_refused` names it. Third-party code runs beside the live Steam login here, so it is pinned (see "Policy for the unattended path"). The cache key covers each asset's repository, tag, id and digest (or upload time without one), so an asset re-uploaded under the same tag is fetched again, and the release API's sha256 digest is checked on every cached and downloaded file. A repeat run downloads nothing (the log prints `Release assets downloaded in this run: N`), and the rig never fetches a manifest. Outbound traffic is blocked by one runner firewall rule per exe found in the game install (the game, the updater, `CrashReportClient.exe` and anything else there), each rule read back after it is made. A per-program rule limits what the game's own programs reach; it is not a sandbox.

| Input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `branch` | `public` (default) or `public_test_branch` |
| `tags` | `Name=tag` overrides, space separated. Names: `Loader`, `BetterCheats`, `BetterDrone`, `CameraControls`, `Codex`, `Compass`, `MiniMap`, `ProductionViewer`, `RuptureTimer`, `WAILA`, `WaveOptimiser`. A plugin of another author (MiniMap) accepts only its reviewed tag; any other tag fails the run |
| `candidate_run_id`, `candidate_artifact` | optional, together: an artifact of a run in this repository whose code came from this repository (a fork's run is refused), laid over the release set. Either the game folder's layout (`dwmapi.dll`, `ModLoader/...`, `ModLoader/Plugins/*.dll`) or the flat layout the build workflows produce: `<Name>.dll` at the artifact root is a plugin (installed in `ModLoader/Plugins/`), `dwmapi.dll` and the loader's own files (Core, ImGui, Updater) go where the loader build puts them. Nothing else is accepted |
| `expect` | `Name=version` the log must show instead of the release tag. Required for every DLL a candidate replaces, or the run fails before launching. A name that is not one of the ten is an extra plugin to expect |
| `expect_refused` | plugins that must be refused on this build; they pass only if refused |
| `expect_decline` | `true` when the build is one the loader's map has no row for: the rig passes only on a clean decline (version-mismatch line, no plugin loaded, no crash, game still running). Not with `expect_refused` |
| `remove_plugins` | plugins left out of the install but still expected, so they must show as missing |

The Steam login is live while candidate code runs, so the rig only runs candidates built from our own branches (the msantoro12 and AlienXAXS repositories). It never runs a fork pull request or anything built straight from issue text.

Dispatch it: `gh workflow run sr-client-rig.yml --ref main -f branch=public`. The outputs are `verdict` (PASS or FAIL), `reason`, `review` (the `Name=tag` of each pinned plugin that has a newer release than the reviewed one, space separated, empty when none) and `artifact` (the scrubbed logs and the verdict's files: `modloader.log`, `proxy.log`, `autoupdate.log`, `verdict.json`, `verdict.txt`, `dll-hashes.json`, `set.json`, `boot.json` and any `compat-report-<CL>.json`; 3 days). The artifact is named `sr-client-rig-<branch>-<candidate artifact, or release>-<run id>-<attempt>`: a called rig has its caller's run id, and the client check runs two rigs per call (sr-watch up to two calls), so the branch and the candidate are in the name. The job fails on a FAIL verdict, after the upload. Game files, dumps, engine logs and Steam config files never leave the runner. Nothing taken from the logs reaches the console, the job summary or an upload before the leak gate has passed: the verdict writes its text to files and the last step publishes them once the gate is green. The gate also covers the Steam persona name, read from what the Steam client wrote after login; if it cannot be determined, nothing from the logs is uploaded or published and the job says why. An always-run step runs `ci/steam-cleanup.ps1`: it removes the login (steamcmd, the Steam config, `loginusers.vdf`, `ssfn*`, the Steam profile, the registry entries; fatal if any stays), then the Steam folder (retried for about 60 s; a folder that stays locked is a warning naming the process holding it). Without the login secrets the run fails with that reason; it does not skip green.

Call it from another workflow in this repository, and only with a candidate built from our own branches. A caller must never pass a fork pull request's build or anything built straight from issue text, because the Steam login is live while the candidate runs:

```yaml
jobs:
  rig:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/sr-client-rig.yml
    with:
      branch: public_test_branch
      candidate_run_id: ${{ needs.build.outputs.run_id }}
      candidate_artifact: loader-client
      expect: Loader=1.22.0-gss.3
    secrets:
      STEAM_CI_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.STEAM_CI_USERNAME }}
      STEAM_CI_LOGIN_CACHE: ${{ secrets.STEAM_CI_LOGIN_CACHE }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
  after:
    needs: rig
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "${{ needs.rig.outputs.verdict }}: ${{ needs.rig.outputs.reason }}"
```

`sr-data-extract.yml` (called from another workflow in this repository, or dispatched) launches the game once with Dumper-7 to make a build's `.usmap`, runs the planner's extractor on the paks and uploads both as `sr-data-<branch>-<buildid>`. Its output `status` is `ok`, `login-failed`, `usmap-failed`, `cleanup-failed` or `extract-failed`; the reason text is never empty. The extractor is planner code, so it never runs while the Steam login is on the runner: after the dump, `ci/steam-cleanup.ps1 -Phase Login` stops every Steam process and service, removes the login material (credentials and tokens: steamcmd, Steam's `config` and `userdata`, `ssfn*`, `config.vdf`, `loginusers.vdf`, the profile and registry entries), retrying each removal for about 60 s, and checks that each piece is gone. If it cannot, the status is `cleanup-failed` with the item and the process holding it in the reason, the extractor does not run (the usmap is still uploaded) and the job fails. `login-failed` is only for a launch that could not sign in. Steam's `logs` folder (account name and connection records, no credential) goes with the folder. `extract-failed` means the extractor ran and failed, or the leak gate or the upload did. The Steam install folder, logs included, is removed last (`-Phase Folder`, after the upload): it retries for about 60 s, and a folder that stays locked is only a warning that names the process holding it. The game itself installs in `INSTALL_DIR` (`D:\sr-client`), outside the Steam folder.

The caller must run on `main` of this repository: the job uses the environment `steam-client`, whose deployment policy serves `main` only, and the caller's permissions must grant `contents: read` and `actions: read`. The caller must pass both Steam secrets by name, as above, even though they exist only in `steam-client`: a called job sees an environment secret only when its caller passes it, and an unpassed one reads as empty with no warning. Both are declared `required`, so a caller that leaves them out fails when the call is parsed. `secrets: inherit` would pass them too, but it hands the called workflow every secret. Runs queue on the concurrency group `sr-client-rig` (one Steam session per account) and are not cancelled, but GitHub keeps only one pending run per group, so a third run replaces a second that is still waiting.

### The rig as the unattended path's gate

The owner's decision: version updates are verified and deployed through this rig. `sr-client-check.yml` calls it twice per candidate, with `needs: [map-mode, candidate-loader]` (a candidate exists only for a build the chain staged and pushed):

| Job | Branch | Inputs |
|---|---|---|
| `rig-branch` | the Steam branch this check is for | `candidate_run_id` = this run, `candidate_artifact` and `expect` = the `candidate-loader` outputs, `expect_refused` = the `map-mode` output; no `tags`: the Latest releases of the plugins of msantoro12 and AlienXAXS, the reviewed release of each plugin of another author |
| `rig-other` | the other one (`public` and `public_test_branch`) | the same, with `expect_refused` = the `map-mode` output `expect_refused_other` (what the loader's own rule predicts for that branch's current build, plus the plugins whose interface the candidate loader does not accept) and `expect_decline` = `expect_decline_other` (that branch's build has no row in the candidate map); needs `rig-branch` and runs after it even if it failed |

They are sequenced because the rig's concurrency group keeps one pending run, so two queued calls would cancel one. The rule for the other branch: `rig-other` declares exactly the refusals the loader's own rule predicts for the other branch's current build (`decide.mjs --other-cl`, output `expect_refused_other`), and any refusal the rule does not predict is a fail, because that branch's current build must keep working with the same DLLs. A plugin the scanner marks REFUSED (its interface is outside the candidate loader's range) is declared on both branches: the same loader runs on both. The other branch's CL comes from its Steam build id (the watcher passes it as `other_buildid`; a dispatch without it reads the branch's live id from Steam with the poll's code, `poll-steam.mjs --live-buildid`, and stops the chain with a message if it cannot; an explicit `other_buildid` wins), looked up in the build rows of the candidate's version map. Example: while the other branch runs CL-129402 and `public` CL-127004, a `public` check declares MiniMap (interface v70, built for CL-127004) for `rig-other`, and a check of the other branch declares nothing for `public`, where MiniMap loads. When no build row has that id the loader has no map for the build and declines it, so `rig-other` is told to expect a clean decline (`decide.mjs --other-unmapped`, output `expect_decline_other`, rig input `expect_decline`): it passes only if the loader logs the version mismatch, loads no plugin, does not crash and the game is still running at the end. Anything else fails the rig. Limit: a plugin of interface v72 or later that is not built here (a released DLL) has no known migration flag, so the rule cannot predict it for another build; a refusal of it on the other branch stays a fail. A rig fail fails its job; `rig-gate` writes the decision, the candidate and both rigs' verdict, reason and logs artifact into the run summary and exits 1 unless both passed, also when a rig never ran for a staged candidate. `publish` needs both rigs with result `success` and verdict `PASS`; with `state/autopilot.json` disabled, publish is held as before and the rigs still run on the candidate. The promote step in `map-mode` only writes a plan, so `publish` is the one place that gates.

What a caller needs: the job runs in environment `steam-client`, which serves `main` only, so the whole run must be on `main`; the call jobs set no environment, pass both Steam secrets by name and ask for `contents: read` and `actions: read`; `sr-watch.yml`'s `client-check` job grants `actions: read` as the ceiling. Nesting is `sr-watch` -> `sr-client-check` -> `sr-client-rig` (two levels of called workflow).

What it does not cover: `-nullrhi` and `[UI] Enabled=0` mean no rendering, so the overlay, the config page and every UI path are not exercised. Plugins are loaded and survive 60 seconds of boot; in-game behaviour is not tested.

### Policy for the unattended path

- **The client rig is a required gate.** It runs the CI's own candidate loader on both Steam branches with the same DLLs. A rig fail blocks publish and raises the alert.
- **Graphics are not a gate.** The rig runs `-nullrhi` to the main menu: no rendering, no overlay, no DX11 and no in-world checks. Graphical problems get small fixes after a release.
- **Autopilot off means build everything, publish nothing.** With `state/autopilot.json` disabled the pipeline still builds, checks and stages every candidate and runs both rigs, and holds only the publish. With the autopilot off the decision stays `HOLD` and the `publish` job is skipped ("publish skipped"). Switched on, a `public` run that passes every gate (decide `M`, publishable, both rigs `PASS`) publishes by itself, signed with the release key in the `vmap-sign` environment (`VMAP_SIGN_KEY`), and the feed carries every build in the loader's map; see `ci/MAP-MODE.md`, "The publish path". The owner turned the autopilot on on 2026-11-10 (path M only). The push of the staged branch needs the deploy key of the loader fork (`ci/MAP-MODE.md`, step 26).
- **Own branches only.** The rig runs only candidates built in this repository from our own branches (msantoro12 and AlienXAXS), never a fork pull request or anything built from issue text, because the Steam login is live while the code runs.
- **The rig is told what it will see.** `expect_refused` is computed from the exact DLLs a rig call will run, not from the plugin builds the check judges: the `check` job resolves the rig's own set (`ci/client-rig-set.ps1`: the Latest released plugins of MOD_OWNER, AlienXAXS by default, and the pinned release of each other author's), fetches it through the rig's download cache (asset id and digest in the key, so the rig then downloads nothing), reads each DLL with `sr-aobscan --plugin` (interface version, the build it names, the loader's note) into `out/rig-plugins.json`, and `decide.mjs --rig-plugins` applies the loader's own refusal rule to those facts. The resolved tags go to both rigs as `tags`, so both run exactly these releases. A DLL whose facts cannot be read has no row and nothing is declared for it, so a refusal of it fails the rig loudly; nothing is guessed. Limit: an asset re-uploaded under the same tag between the check and the rig is not caught for the plugins of msantoro12 and AlienXAXS (the pinned plugins are digest-checked by the rig).
- **Expected refusals on the other branch.** `rig-other` declares only what the loader's own rule predicts for the other branch's current build; any refusal the rule does not predict is a fail (see above).
- **Plugins of other authors are pinned.** A plugin whose owner is neither msantoro12 nor AlienXAXS (MiniMap, and LetMeInside in `ci/plugin-names.json`) runs only at a reviewed release, in the rig and in the client check alike (the check job's `plugin-plan` reads the same `Pin`, fetches that tag, requires its client DLL to carry the Pin's digest, and never builds such a plugin from source; a Pin that is missing or malformed, or a digest that differs, costs only that plugin its scan as FETCH-FAILED, so unreviewed code never runs next to the Steam login): its entry carries `Pin` = `{ "Tag": "<release tag>", "Digest": "sha256:<64 hex>" }`, the tag and the release API's digest of its client DLL as reviewed. The rig fetches that tag, and a digest that differs on the pinned tag fails the run (the asset changed after review). An entry without a Pin, or with a malformed one, fails the run before any release is read, and a `tags` override naming another tag fails it too. The nine plugins of msantoro12 and AlienXAXS keep resolving Latest. When the author's Latest release is not the pinned tag, the rig still runs the pinned one, and the run raises "new <plugin> release <tag> waiting for review" through the alert job (the `review` output of `plugin-plan` and of both rigs); that line blocks nothing and the chain still counts as passed. To accept the new release, read it, then replace the Pin's tag and digest in `ci/plugin-names.json` (the digest is on the release API: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/tags/<tag>`).

## Testing the update path

1. Seed: `gh workflow run sr-watch.yml`. Expect a green run, "Seeded baseline" in the summary, no PR, and `state/steam.json` on main.
2. Commit an older client public `buildid` into `state/steam.json` on main, then run the watcher again.
3. Expect: a `game-update/...` PR with the checklist, a `build-all` run, and when it finishes a PR comment with one row per component.
4. Merge the PR; main holds the current ids again.

## Limits

- `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot act on other repositories, so nothing here dispatches or edits a mod repo.
- A PR opened with `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not start other workflows, so the watcher calls `sr-build-all.yml` with `workflow_call`.
- A scheduled workflow is switched off after 60 days without repository activity. `sr-keepalive.yml` runs monthly and calls the workflow `enable` API (`actions: write`, no push) for `sr-watch.yml`, `sr-build-all.yml`, `sr-client-check.yml` and itself, which resets the timer. It is a plain `gh api` call, not a third-party action.
- Persistent API trouble is a log warning, not a red run; look for "SKIPPED (API failure)" in the summary.
- None of the mod repos' release workflows are called or referenced from here.
